question.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{′}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{′}}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x(\frac{1}{x})}{{ln}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{-x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{x{ln}^{2}⁡x}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
